title: JavaBinaryLauncher::CreateClasspathJar() fails on Windows if manifest_jar_path or jar_manifest_file_path contain spaces
body:
### Description of the bug:


Windows escaping was forgotten in `JavaBinaryLauncher::CreateClasspathJar()`. As result, incorrect arguments were passed to `BinaryLauncherBase::LaunchProcess`.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


Run a scenario where classpath JAR is required on Windows and the corresponding path contains spaces. 

The easiest way to reach it - create a Java project which will be compiled with Bazel on the path with spaces and try to build and to launch it via Bazel. 
It can be non-trivial to create a test project which will require classpath jar creation, so the easiest way to check the problem is getting rid of `if (classpath_str.length() > this->classpath_limit)` condition at https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/8028655414a189b6897b1b51e3e43b5711e0af98/src/tools/launcher/java_launcher.cc#L389


### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Windows

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


according to official guide + set BAZEL_SH environment variable to "c:/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe", because by default WSL version of bash was used -`C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text
git@github.com:bazelbuild/bazel.git
00b48b27aa216befc419e540919a1f1df4cda337
```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


it's not a regression

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

_No response_
